      "title": "Refactor Skillplane into a global control plane and regional workspace cells",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-13/refactor-skillplane-into-a-global-control-plane-and-regional-workspace",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nRefactor Skillplane into a global gateway/control plane plus regional workspace cells while preserving the canonical public endpoints `app.skillplane.dev` and `mcp.skillplane.dev`. Clients, OAuth callbacks, and MCP integrations must not resolve or switch to regional hostnames.\n\nThe gateway/control plane owns globally required identity and workspace-routing state. Each workspace is assigned to exactly one regional cell that owns its tenant data and bundle storage. Requests are routed internally using the AuthFn and DataFn multi-region contracts, with provider-neutral application interfaces and Cloudflare-specific adapters confined to deployment packages.\n\n## Current implementation basis\n\nVerified against current Skillplane branch/remote head `SKI-8` at `3de271619200f9ee45fd31ee056568f8500b7db5`:\n\n* `packages/config/src/index.ts` accepts one `HYPERDRIVE` binding and one `SKILL_BUNDLES` object-storage binding and produces one database/runtime configuration.\n* `packages/api/src/services.ts` constructs AuthFn, DataFn, domain services, and R2 repositories around the same database client and bucket.\n* `packages/auth/src/server.ts` configures AuthFn without its multi-region plugin; `packages/datafn/src/server.ts` configures one DataFn database and derives the namespace from the authenticated workspace.\n* `packages/db/src/schema/domain.ts` co-locates AuthFn identity, workspaces/memberships/invitations/service principals, and workspace content. It uses database foreign keys across those categories.\n* `packages/api/src/tenancy.ts` joins workspace membership directly to `authfn_users` and creates personal workspaces transactionally in the same database.\n* The MCP OAuth implementation stores opaque authorization codes, access tokens, refresh tokens, clients, and consent records in the same PostgreSQL origin.\n* `scripts/render-deploy-config.mjs` and production deployment helpers require exactly one Hyperdrive configuration, one R2 bucket, and one custom-domain route per app/MCP worker.\n* Production issuer/resource are already canonical: `https://app.skillplane.dev` and `https://mcp.skillplane.dev/mcp`.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe current process and relational schema assume every request, user, workspace, skill, OAuth record, and bundle is reachable through one database/storage pair. Adding a second region cannot be solved by DNS alone: clients do not always know the workspace before authentication, OAuth callbacks must retain a stable issuer, users may belong to workspaces in multiple regions, and cross-database foreign keys cannot span regional cells.\n\nA canonical gateway removes regional-hostname resolution from clients, but it becomes a global dependency. If ingress or the authoritative workspace directory is unavailable, healthy cells cannot be reached through the canonical endpoints. The architecture must make this dependency explicit, replicated/cached where safe, observable, and fail-closed rather than silently selecting a region.\n\n## Target architecture\n\n### Global gateway/control plane\n\nThe canonical app and MCP workers terminate public HTTP/TLS, enforce request size and abuse controls, attach correlation identity, and dispatch internally. The global control plane owns the minimum state required before a workspace cell can be selected:\n\n* AuthFn account placement and canonical session/OAuth routing metadata;\n* users and global identity references;\n* workspace directory: workspace ID/slug, owning region, routing epoch, lifecycle state;\n* workspace membership and invitation routing metadata needed to determine authorized workspace access;\n* service-principal/API-key-to-workspace mapping;\n* OAuth client registration, authorization request/code, consent, token family/revocation state, or another explicitly documented globally reachable partition;\n* global publication/search projection needed for unauthenticated or cross-workspace discovery;\n* placement/migration audit records and gateway configuration.\n\nThis is a logical control-plane boundary, not necessarily one primary database. Its backing services must satisfy the documented consistency/availability contract.\n\n### Regional workspace cell\n\nEach cell owns one regional PostgreSQL/DataFn instance and regional object storage for assigned workspaces, including:\n\n* skills, versions, files, contexts, notes, amendments, reviews, publication state, tenant audit/idempotency records, and other workspace-domain tables;\n* bundle objects and digests for those workspaces;\n* cell-local indexes, queues, and outboxes;\n* no authority to assign a workspace to itself without an atomic global placement claim.\n\nA workspace has one writable home region at a time. Active-active writes for one workspace are out of scope.\n\n## Required work\n\n### 1. Create explicit platform interfaces\n\nIntroduce provider-neutral application contracts for:\n\n* `WorkspacePlacementDirectory` with atomic create and compare-and-set move semantics;\n* `RegionalCellRegistry`/dispatcher using adapter-owned internal handles;\n* signed `RoutingAssertion` containing workspace, region, epoch, request ID, expiry, and replay protection;\n* control-plane and cell service factories;\n* global vs regional database clients and object-storage resolvers.\n\nCloudflare implementations may use Workers, Service Bindings, Hyperdrive, R2, Durable Objects, KV, or Queues, but domain/config packages must not import those provider APIs. Document an alternative deployment shape using ordinary HTTP/RPC plus another strongly consistent directory.\n\n### 2. Split the schema by ownership\n\nClassify every current table as global, regional, replicated projection, or migration-only. Remove cross-boundary database foreign keys and replace them with stable opaque IDs plus service-level validation/audit.\n\nPay special attention to:\n\n* personal-workspace creation;\n* membership/invitation acceptance;\n* service-principal issuance/revocation;\n* OAuth authorization, refresh rotation, and token verification;\n* public skill publication/search;\n* audit attribution that references users;\n* idempotency records and concurrency tokens.\n\nAdd contract tests proving referential and authorization invariants after physical separation.\n\n### 3. Route app and MCP requests without client hostname changes\n\nKeep all externally advertised origins canonical. The gateway must derive routing from trusted context:\n\n* pre-auth account lookup for OTP/sign-in via AuthFn;\n* authenticated workspace selection from URL/session/tool input and global membership state;\n* service-principal token mapping;\n* public skill lookup through a global projection or deterministic publication directory.\n\nThe gateway forwards through an internal service adapter. Clients never receive internal regional origins. Unknown, unauthorized, moving, stale, and unavailable states return distinct safe errors.\n\nFor MCP, preserve OAuth resource discovery and token audience at `mcp.skillplane.dev/mcp`; route individual tool calls only after validating the token and requested workspace/skill context.\n\n### 4. Integrate AuthFn and DataFn plugins\n\nAdopt the gateway mode from the AuthFn multi-region issue for canonical identity/OAuth/session routing and the DataFn multi-region issue for workspace namespace placement/execution fencing.\n\nSkillplane-specific code should be thin plugin/config composition:\n\n* AuthFn multi-region runtime adapter and global lookup store;\n* DataFn multi-region placement/directory adapter;\n* request-context bridge that turns validated global identity + workspace membership into a short-lived cell assertion;\n* cell-local service construction from resolved bindings.\n\nDo not fork AuthFn/DataFn routing logic into Skillplane.\n\n### 5. Refactor runtime and deployment configuration\n\nReplace singular assumptions with an explicit topology manifest that identifies the control plane, cells, database/storage bindings, internal destinations, and routing keys. Validate:\n\n* duplicate or unknown region IDs;\n* missing cell/database/bucket bindings;\n* issuer/resource drift from canonical origins;\n* directory credentials and signing-key rotation;\n* no public route exposure for cell-only workers;\n* per-cell least-privilege secrets.\n\nUpdate deployment, smoke, rollback, backup/restore, local development, and disaster-recovery tooling. Generated configuration must support one control plane plus at least two cells.\n\n### 6. Regional object storage and publication\n\nUse workspace-aware bundle keys and resolve the owning bucket from placement. Define whether public bundles remain in-cell behind gateway streaming, are copied to a global publication bucket/CDN, or use a replicated immutable publication layer. Document residency, cache invalidation, digest verification, deletion, and restore behavior.\n\nDo not describe R2 as region-pinned unless the selected Cloudflare product/configuration actually guarantees the required residency; residency must be an explicit verified deployment capability.\n\n### 7. Migration and rollout\n\nUse a staged rollout:\n\n1. add global IDs/directory and routing epoch while remaining single-cell;\n2. split interfaces and remove cross-boundary foreign keys;\n3. run canonical gateway against the original cell;\n4. provision a second cell and place only new test/internal workspaces there;\n5. place new customer workspaces by policy;\n6. build an explicit workspace migration workflow before moving existing workspaces.\n\nMigration must fence writes, copy database and bundles, verify counts/digests/invariants, atomically advance the epoch, warm caches, resume traffic, and retain rollback evidence. Never fail over a workspace to an empty cell merely because its home is unhealthy.\n\n### 8. Reliability, security, and observability\n\nDefine SLOs and runbooks for global ingress, placement directory, each cell, and internal dispatch. Cache signed placement decisions briefly, but fail closed on unknown/stale ownership. Support independent cell deploy/rollback and blast-radius isolation.\n\nEmit safe metrics/logs for routing decisions, directory latency, cache hit, mismatch/retry, cell health, migration phase, cross-region latency, and storage operations. Never log raw OTPs, OAuth secrets, API keys, bearer tokens, or unnecessary email identifiers.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `app.skillplane.dev` and `mcp.skillplane.dev` remain the only client-required production hosts.\n- [ ] Browser OTP auth, sessions, OAuth authorization/refresh/revocation, MCP calls, and service-principal calls work for workspaces in two cells without client-side regional resolution.\n- [ ] One user can access authorized workspaces in different regions through the same session/canonical origins.\n- [ ] The global directory atomically assigns each workspace to one region and exposes a routing epoch; stale gateways are fenced before cell side effects.\n- [ ] The schema has an approved table-by-table ownership map and no cross-database foreign-key assumptions.\n- [ ] Regional cells cannot trust caller-supplied workspace/region headers; they validate a short-lived signed assertion and local placement epoch.\n- [ ] Public skill retrieval/search has a documented cross-region projection path with tested publication/update/delete semantics.\n- [ ] Bundles for each workspace resolve to the intended regional/global publication storage with digest verification and documented residency guarantees.\n- [ ] A generated/deployed test topology supports one control plane plus two cells using provider-specific adapters behind provider-neutral interfaces.\n- [ ] Directory/control-plane and one-cell outage scenarios have tested safe errors, cache behavior, alerting, and recovery; no request is routed to a random/default cell.\n- [ ] New workspaces can be placed in either cell; existing workspaces remain on the original cell until the migration workflow passes verification.\n- [ ] Workspace migration proves write fencing, database count/invariant checks, bundle digest checks, atomic epoch switch, rollback evidence, and client transparency.\n- [ ] Existing single-cell local development and deployment remain supported during the transition.\n- [ ] Security, conformance, integration, load, and failover tests cover app, MCP, AuthFn, DataFn, and storage boundaries.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nThis product refactor depends on reusable gateway-mode support in AuthFn and namespace-placement/gateway support in DataFn. It should consume those interfaces as plugins/adapters rather than implementing product-local substitutes.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Active-active writes for one workspace.\n* Replacing canonical app/MCP origins with public regional hostnames.\n* Coupling Skillplane's domain layer to Cloudflare-only APIs.\n* Automatic data migration or failover without fencing and verification.\n* Making every table globally replicated.",

      "id": "e1f5f8da-816f-4405-b3eb-9c02de4ad1bd",
      "identifier": "SKI-14",
      "title": "Adapt Skillplane tool contracts for authenticated client compatibility",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-14/adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-for-authenticated-client-compatibility",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdapt Skillplane's McpFn integration so model-visible tool schemas contain only model-owned arguments, trusted caller attribution is injected before validation, workspace selectors are consistent, and pre-handler validation failures are observable and actionable.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nThe production MCP endpoint successfully authenticated a hosted client and advertised the tool catalog, but a request to list available skills failed strict validation before reaching the handler. No tool audit record was created because the failure occurred at the schema boundary.\n\nSkillplane currently exposes a required multi-field `caller` object in its canonical tool schemas. One existing client-specific path removes that field from `tools/list` and restores trusted attribution during `tools/call`; other hosted clients receive the unadapted schema. Skill discovery also uses inconsistent workspace shapes: `skills_list` expects a nested workspace selector while `skills_search` expects a flat workspace identifier. These differences increase the chance that a model generates a valid-looking but incompatible root shape.\n\nThe current validation response reports only a generic additional-properties error at the root and discards the rejected property name, making production diagnosis unnecessarily difficult.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nEvery supported authenticated client receives an intentional, tested catalog projection. Server-owned attribution comes only from verified request context, tool-selection flows use consistent workspace selectors, and deterministic tests prove that catalog projection and call enrichment remain symmetrical. Failures before handler execution produce safe structured diagnostics and audit evidence.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Resolve client profile from verified authentication context rather than self-reported client metadata.\n* Remove server-owned caller fields from model-visible tool input schemas.\n* Inject trusted caller attribution before strict validation and handler execution.\n* Replace the one-off client adaptation with an explicit, reviewed profile policy.\n* Normalize or deliberately version workspace-selector conventions across discovery tools.\n* Adopt the reusable deterministic profile contract supplied by McpFn.\n* Record redacted pre-handler validation failures with request and profile correlation.\n* Preserve approved tool behavior, tenancy, scopes, authorization, and audit semantics.\n* Add deployed verification for the affected skill-listing journey.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Relax `additionalProperties: false` globally.\n* Trust caller attribution supplied by a model or unverified client.\n* Move Skillplane tenancy, grants, approval, or domain policy into McpFn.\n* Rework the authorization-code or token lifecycle.\n* Duplicate protocol conformance coverage.\n* Treat a model-generated evaluation as deterministic proof.\n* Implement unrelated tool catalog redesign.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Supported hosted clients receive documented profile-specific `tools/list` output selected from verified request context.\n* Model-visible schemas do not require the server-owned `caller` object.\n* `tools/call` injects authenticated caller attribution before strict validation and ignores or rejects forged caller metadata according to one documented policy.\n* `workspaces_list`, `skills_list`, and `skills_search` support a documented skill-discovery sequence with one consistent workspace-selector convention, or a versioned compatibility plan is approved.\n* A deterministic red/green regression preserves the original list-skills incident's effective `tools/list` schema and redacted rejected `tools/call.params.arguments`, proves the pre-fix path fails, proves the corrected catalog projection plus trusted enrichment reaches the handler and returns the skill list, and retains the malformed call as a negative diagnostic test that names the rejected property.\n* Tests fail when catalog projection and call enrichment become asymmetric.\n* An unexpected root property produces structured diagnostics containing the exact rejected property and validation location without exposing sensitive argument values.\n* A validation failure before handler execution produces a redacted audit or diagnostic event with request correlation.\n* The existing adapted client path and service-principal behavior remain covered.\n* Existing unit, integration, security, MCP contract, conformance, and production smoke gates remain green.\n* As a separate non-deterministic deployed canary, controlled deployed verification runs the original list-skills prompt through a real target-family model using the configured client profile and asserts successful tool execution and the returned response. Hosted inference or API-key access is sufficient; no account or login to the client application is required.\n* Rollback does not silently restore a catalog that exposes server-owned required fields to model clients.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Immediate Skillplane compatibility remediation is independent of [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema). [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema) remains required before replacing the local profile lifecycle with the reusable McpFn profile and schema-diagnostic contract.\n* Related to the completed McpFn runtime adoption, but addresses a newly observed post-adoption compatibility gap.\n* Changing public input schemas can affect cached catalogs and existing clients; rollout and cache invalidation must be explicit.\n* Uniform server-owned attribution is safer, but legacy direct callers may need a bounded migration path.\n* Workspace-selector normalization may be a behavioral schema change and requires compatibility review.\n* Diagnostic events must never record credentials, tokens, full prompts, or sensitive tool arguments.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should caller attribution be removed from every public tool schema or only from model-facing projections during a transition?\n* Which existing direct callers still submit caller metadata, and what migration window do they require?\n* Should workspace selection use one nested selector everywhere or one flat identifier everywhere?\n* Where should safe pre-handler validation events be retained and for how long?\n* Which deployed environments must pass the client-profile canary before production rollout?\n\n## Detailed documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale \u2014 SKI-14](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-14-adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-08f4c3c72edd>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan \u2014 SKI-14](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-14-adapt-skillplane-tool-contracts-95429a5fc9ec>)",

      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-skillplane-mcp-runtime-authorization-and-quality-gates",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nFully adopt McpFn for Skillplane's production MCP runtime, MCP-specific hosted authorization compatibility, regression testing, and official conformance. Skillplane should retain product domain behavior, tenancy, grants, consent policy, and token-authority dependencies while removing its product-local MCP protocol, client-metadata, compatible-flow, redirect-validation, and test-harness implementations.\n\nThis issue absorbs the required production outcome from [SKI-5](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-5/accept-extensible-oauth-client-metadata-for-claude-and-other-mcp). [SKI-5](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-5/accept-extensible-oauth-client-metadata-for-claude-and-other-mcp) is canceled as superseded only because valid Claude and ChatGPT login behavior becomes an explicit acceptance requirement here and in [MCP-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform).\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkillplane currently owns MCP and OAuth behavior that should become shared McpFn capability:\n\n* its Client ID Metadata Document hydration and dynamic-registration paths share strict registration validation;\n* grant compatibility is evaluated against the client's complete advertised grant set instead of the flow requested now;\n* redirect URI behavior and deployment registration can drift independently;\n* project-specific MCP tests do not invoke the official MCP conformance runner;\n* McpFn is not used as the production server/authorization compatibility layer;\n* retaining Skillplane-local role-3 logic after [MCP-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform) would create two implementations that can diverge.\n\n[MCP-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform) establishes the ownership boundary:\n\n* McpFn owns the MCP runtime plus MCP-specific protected-resource/authorization-server discovery, pre-registration/DCR/Client ID Metadata Documents, compatible-flow negotiation, redirect rules, PKCE/resource/scope requirements, protocol error mapping, diagnostics, regression, and conformance integration.\n* AuthFn or another underlying security system owns users, login, sessions, tenant/region context, consent policy, signing keys, token authority, and durable security state.\n* Skillplane owns workspace/version/grant/approval/domain policy and supplies those decisions through explicit adapters.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nSkillplane's production MCP endpoint runs through released McpFn server and hosted-authorization contracts. Valid Claude and ChatGPT authorization-code + PKCE logins succeed without Skillplane implementing MCP-specific registration, client-metadata, or redirect-validation rules.\n\nA single production path serves MCP traffic and authorization compatibility. Existing Skillplane behavior is inventoried, migrated, removed, or deliberately retained as a temporary compatibility shim with an owner and removal condition. The same McpFn target/session engine powers deterministic regression, official conformance, and diagnostics.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Pin released McpFn runtime, auth, testing, and CLI packages with an explicit upgrade policy.\n* Migrate Skillplane's MCP server lifecycle and supported transports to McpFn while preserving domain tool contracts.\n* Adopt [MCP-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform)'s hosted-server authorization adapter for protected-resource metadata, authorization-server metadata, client registration modes, Client ID Metadata Documents, compatible-flow negotiation, redirect validation, PKCE, resource indicators, MCP scopes, and protocol errors.\n* Integrate AuthFn or the selected authorization system through a narrow adapter for authenticated identity/session/tenant context; do not treat AuthFn's social OAuth client as an MCP authorization server.\n* Keep Skillplane's grants, workspace/version resolution, approval, consent policy, token authority, signing, and persistence explicit.\n* Inventory overlapping Skillplane, McpFn, AuthFn, shared OAuth, and test code before migration.\n* Reuse generic PKCE/state/HTTP/storage/redaction primitives from shared Superfunctions packages instead of creating another implementation.\n* Remove or deprecate replaced Skillplane MCP/OAuth compatibility paths and prove no unintended production fallback remains.\n* Run McpFn contract, semantic, API-key, OAuth, provider-shaped, and official-conformance suites against Skillplane.\n* Add controlled Claude- and ChatGPT-shaped end-to-end login verification with redacted diagnostics.\n* Separate deterministic pull-request gates, slower conformance, controlled live-provider smokes, and deployed production proof.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Move Skillplane domain authorization, grants, approval workflows, workspace/version policy, or business semantics into McpFn.\n* Implement JWT bearer, device code, or arbitrary extension grants merely because a client advertises them.\n* Make AuthFn mandatory.\n* Claim AuthFn's existing social-login OAuth feature is an MCP authorization server.\n* Reimplement generic identity, sessions, consent policy, signing, token authority, or durable security storage in McpFn.\n* Introduce an unauthenticated production MCP route.\n* Retain two active production implementations of MCP-specific client metadata, registration, compatible-flow, or redirect validation.\n* Treat a green mock or conformance suite as proof of live-provider or production configuration.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Skillplane installs exact released McpFn versions and records a compatibility/upgrade policy.\n* The production MCP endpoint uses the McpFn server runtime for lifecycle and supported transports without changing approved tool names, schemas, result envelopes, or domain errors.\n* The production authorization flow uses the McpFn hosted-server compatibility adapter for pre-registration/DCR/Client ID Metadata Documents, compatible-flow negotiation, redirect matching, PKCE, resource/scope validation, and MCP-shaped errors.\n* Skillplane supplies identity/session/tenant context and token-authority dependencies through explicit adapters; generic identity and security state remain outside McpFn.\n* A Claude-shaped metadata document advertising authorization code, refresh token, and additional registered extension grants completes authorization code + PKCE.\n* A ChatGPT-shaped registered client completes authorization with its actual callback URI.\n* Metadata with no compatible requested flow and a genuinely unregistered callback fail with accurate, phase-specific errors.\n* An actual unsupported token grant remains `unsupported_grant_type`; authorization-server metadata never advertises unimplemented grants.\n* Registration records and authorization requests are independently configured in tests so drift is detectable.\n* A code-ownership inventory names every overlapping MCP client/server, OAuth, auth middleware, storage, and test helper in Skillplane and Superfunctions.\n* Replaced Skillplane role-3 entry points are deleted or explicitly deprecated; the release gate proves only one production validator/writer handles each responsibility and fails if an unintended fallback is used.\n* Shared OAuth PKCE/state/HTTP/storage/redaction primitives are reused where compatible; each retained McpFn- or Skillplane-specific implementation has a documented MCP/domain reason.\n* Existing Skillplane unit/integration coverage remains, while McpFn adds transport-neutral semantic, auth, provider-shaped, and official-conformance coverage.\n* Official MCP conformance runs against an authenticated local Skillplane endpoint without a production auth bypass.\n* CI emits bounded, secret-redacted, machine-readable artifacts that identify discovery, registration, redirect, authorization, token, resource-server, transport, initialization, or scenario failure.\n* Controlled live verification proves Claude and ChatGPT reach consent and complete token exchange through the migrated production integration.\n* Rollback cannot silently restore the removed buggy path; rollback and compatibility-shim behavior are documented and tested.\n* [SKI-5](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-5/accept-extensible-oauth-client-metadata-for-claude-and-other-mcp)'s immediate behavior outcome is completely represented by these criteria before       "id": "82cd67e3-8311-45ec-9b82-033069d90de4",
      "identifier": "SKI-5",
      "title": "Accept extensible OAuth client metadata for Claude and other MCP clients",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-5/accept-extensible-oauth-client-metadata-for-claude-and-other-mcp",
      "description": "## Supersession decision \u2014 2026-08-25\n\n**Status: canceled as superseded, not resolved.** The production defect and its security constraints remain valid, but the implementation is no longer tracked as a Skillplane-local OAuth patch.\n\nThe required behavior is now owned by [MCP-2: Make McpFn the batteries-included MCP SDK and quality platform](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-2/make-mcpfn-the-batteries-included-mcp-sdk-and-quality-platform>) and adopted into Skillplane through [SKI-6: Adopt McpFn for Skillplane MCP runtime, authorization, and quality gates](<https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-skillplane-mcp-runtime-authorization-and-quality-gates>).\n\n[SKI-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-skillplane-mcp-runtime-authorization-and-quality-gates) cannot complete until this issue\u2019s outcome is proven through the McpFn-backed production path: compatible Claude-shaped metadata reaches authorization code + PKCE and token exchange; ChatGPT is verified independently; extra advertised grants do not become enabled; actual unsupported token grants remain rejected; and the historical failure is covered by deterministic regression plus controlled live evidence.\n\nThe root-cause analysis and security requirements below are retained as migration evidence. If full McpFn adoption is abandoned or cannot meet these acceptance requirements, this issue must be reopened or replaced explicitly.\n\n## Executive summary\n\nMake Skillplane's OAuth Client ID Metadata Document handling interoperable with MCP clients that advertise additional registered grant types while using Skillplane's supported authorization-code flow. The immediate failure is Claude authentication returning `invalid_client` because Claude's metadata includes JWT bearer alongside `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`.\n\n## Problem\n\nSkillplane currently uses the same strict registration validator for two different protocols:\n\n* dynamic client registration, where rejecting grants the authorization server cannot register is reasonable;\n* Client ID Metadata Documents, which are client-owned capability descriptions reusable across authorization servers.\n\nThe shared validator rejects the entire metadata document when any advertised grant is outside Skillplane's allowlist. That blocks a valid authorization-code + PKCE request before consent, even though the unsupported grant is not being requested.\n\nArchived observations show Claude metadata advertised only `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` before the implementation, then added `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`. The original synthetic tests covered the former shape but not a supported flow plus a registered extension grant.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA compliant MCP client can authenticate through authorization code + PKCE whenever its metadata provides a compatible supported path, even if the same metadata advertises additional grants for other authorization servers. Actual unsupported token requests remain rejected at the token endpoint.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Separate Client ID Metadata Document compatibility validation from dynamic-registration policy.\n* Validate the capabilities required by the current authorization request rather than requiring the client's full grant set to equal Skillplane's.\n* Preserve exact client identifier and redirect URI checks, public-client policy, PKCE S256, resource binding, scope validation, and SSRF protections.\n* Return accurate, standards-shaped errors for genuinely incompatible metadata and actual unsupported token grants.\n* Add regression coverage using Claude's current metadata shape and generic registered extension grants.\n* Verify the change through unit, integration, security, and live MCP OAuth testing.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Implement JWT bearer token exchange in Skillplane.\n* Expand Skillplane's supported grant types beyond authorization code and refresh token.\n* Relax redirect URI, client identity, scope, resource, PKCE, or token-security controls.\n* Change Claude's published client metadata.\n* Implement or deploy the correction as part of this backlog-capture operation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A metadata document containing `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and a registered extension grant can proceed through authorization code + PKCE.\n* A metadata document without a flow compatible with the authorization request is rejected with an accurate error.\n* An actual token request using JWT bearer remains rejected as `unsupported_grant_type`.\n* Dynamic client registration retains an explicit, documented policy for unsupported requested grants.\n* Client metadata and dynamic-registration validation have distinct tests and responsibilities.\n* Claude authentication reaches consent and completes token exchange in a controlled live verification.\n* Existing OAuth security tests remain green.\n* Authorization-server metadata does not advertise grant support Skillplane does not implement.\n* Operational diagnostics distinguish metadata incompatibility from token-endpoint grant rejection without recording sensitive authorization values.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Standards interpretation should be checked against MCP authorization 2025-11-25, the Client ID Metadata Document draft version it references, RFC 7591 client metadata, and the JWT bearer grant registration.\n* Broadly ignoring metadata can create security regressions; only unknown or unsupported capability declarations should be tolerated while required identity, redirect, authentication-method, and request-specific constraints remain fail-closed.\n* Client metadata is mutable and fetched remotely, so compatibility tests should include provider-shaped fixtures plus a controlled live contract check.\n* Existing metadata caching and database hydration behavior must not preserve an incompatible or partially validated client.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should unknown grant values be ignored, recorded for diagnostics, or rejected unless they are registered OAuth extension grants?\n* Should Client ID Metadata validation require `authorization_code` explicitly or derive compatibility solely from `response_types` and the current request?\n* Should metadata scopes be treated as a client capability set, an upper bound, or ignored in favor of request-time authorization-server scope validation?\n* What cache invalidation and observability are appropriate when a provider changes metadata?\n* Should compatibility contracts cover Claude and other major MCP clients in scheduled production smoke tests?\n\n## Evidence\n\n* Root-cause location: `packages/authfn-mcp-oauth/src/clients.ts`; metadata hydration and dynamic registration both call `validateRegistration`.\n* The grant allowlist rejects any value outside `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`.\n* The token endpoint already independently rejects actual unsupported grants.\n* Existing positive metadata coverage contains exactly Skillplane's supported grants; the negative test only uses a wholly unsupported password grant.",

      "id": "8daff819-16fe-4c7f-aa1b-13012e8c24f9",
      "identifier": "SKI-12",
      "title": "Support Git-hosted skill sources and repository-wide imports",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-12/support-git-hosted-skill-sources-and-repository-wide-imports",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAllow a Skillplane-managed skill to use a Git-hosted skill file as its source of truth, and allow one Git repository to act as a shared source for multiple skills. Expose source-level grouping so users can see every managed skill derived from a given repository or source configuration.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkill authors already maintain canonical skill instructions in Git repositories. Copying those files into Skillplane creates drift, obscures provenance, and makes updates manual. Repository-scale collections such as [vercel-labs/skills](<https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills>) and catalogs surfaced through [skills.sh](<https://skills.sh/>) also need a single import and synchronization model rather than one disconnected setup per skill.\n\nA concrete single-skill example is Diffpanel's repository file at `skills/diffpanel-chapters/SKILL.md`.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA workspace can register a Git source once, map one file to one managed skill or discover multiple skills from a repository, synchronize immutable Skillplane versions from exact Git revisions, and inspect all skills grouped by their common source.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Represent a Git source with repository identity, provider, ref policy, credentials where needed, and provenance.\n* Configure an individual managed skill from one Git-hosted `SKILL.md` path.\n* Import or synchronize multiple skills from a repository containing a skill collection.\n* Track each published Skillplane version back to an exact commit and source path.\n* Show and filter all skills associated with the same source.\n* Detect changes, additions, removals, renames, failures, and drift without silently overwriting managed state.\n* Support public repositories first while preserving a secure path for private repositories.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Executing arbitrary repository code during import.\n* Treating a mutable branch name alone as immutable provenance.\n* Automatically deleting managed skills when upstream files disappear.\n* General-purpose Git hosting or repository mirroring.\n* Assuming every repository follows one directory layout.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A user can configure a single source using repository URL, ref policy, and `SKILL.md` path.\n* A successful synchronization records the resolved commit SHA, source path, content digest, timestamp, and outcome.\n* Repository-wide import discovers supported skills deterministically and previews changes before applying them.\n* One source detail view lists every managed skill sourced from it, including sync and drift status.\n* Repeated synchronization of the same commit and content is idempotent and does not create duplicate versions.\n* Changed content creates a reviewable candidate or published version according to the skill's existing publication policy.\n* Missing, renamed, malformed, or conflicting source files produce explicit non-destructive states.\n* Repository content is treated as untrusted input: path traversal, symlink escape, oversized bundles, unsupported files, and secret exposure are prevented.\n* Existing manually managed skills remain unchanged until explicitly connected to a source.\n* Source removal does not erase immutable Skillplane version history.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing immutable bundle/version, amendment review, visibility, tenancy, audit, and credential models.\n* Git provider API limits, webhook reliability, force-pushes, deleted refs, and private repository authorization.\n* Repository discovery conventions and conflicts between source metadata and Skillplane metadata.\n* Supply-chain risks from compromised repositories or mutable refs.\n* Scale limits for large monorepos and bulk synchronization.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which providers and URL forms are supported first?\n* Are refs pinned to commits, tracked branches/tags, or both?\n* Is synchronization manual, scheduled, webhook-driven, or configurable?\n* What repository layouts and manifests define multiple skills?\n* How are upstream rename and deletion intents confirmed?\n* Can one managed skill combine Git-sourced files with Skillplane-managed overlays?\n* How are forks and repository transfers represented without losing provenance?\n* Should [skills.sh](<http://skills.sh>) be integrated as a catalog/discovery layer, a Git source resolver, or both?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-25abc9c35487>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-12-support-git-hosted-skill-sources-20057351abbe>)",

      "id": "9cb0acc8-c438-416f-9ddf-048fcfe1a882",
      "identifier": "SKI-11",
      "title": "Support skill groups and workspace member assignments",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-11/support-skill-groups-and-workspace-member-assignments",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdd workspace-level skill groups so Skillplane can organize related skills by domain and associate workspace members with those groups\u2014for example Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nA flat workspace skill catalog does not express which skills belong together or which members should work with a domain-specific collection. As the catalog and workspace membership grow, discovery, onboarding, and administration become harder.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nWorkspace administrators can define reusable skill groups, associate skills and members with them, and inspect those relationships. Members can quickly find the skills relevant to their domains.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Create, rename, describe, archive, and restore skill groups within a workspace.\n* Associate skills with skill groups.\n* Associate workspace members with skill groups.\n* Show and filter skills and members by group.\n* Preserve workspace isolation, role-based administration, auditability, and deterministic API behavior.\n* Define how group membership interacts with skill visibility and authorization before rollout.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Replacing existing workspace roles.\n* Inferring a member's group from job title or behavior.\n* Automatically generating or changing skill content.\n* Implementing organization-wide groups shared across unrelated workspaces unless separately designed.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A workspace can maintain domain groups such as Design, Marketing, Development, and Sales.\n* Authorized administrators can add and remove skills and members without duplicate associations.\n* Group detail views expose the associated skills and members; skill/member views expose their groups.\n* Lists and search can filter by group.\n* Archived groups do not silently delete skills, members, or historical audit records.\n* Cross-workspace references are rejected.\n* Every membership change is attributable in audit history.\n* Existing workspaces continue to work without creating groups.\n* Product and API semantics clearly state whether groups are organizational only or affect effective skill access.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Existing workspace membership, skill visibility, authorization, and audit models.\n* Risk of accidentally widening access if group membership is treated as a grant.\n* Risk of confusing group membership with workspace role or team ownership.\n* Migration and indexing requirements for existing skills and members.\n* Large groups may require pagination and bulk-operation safeguards.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Does membership grant skill access, configure defaults, or only categorize and filter?\n* Can a skill and a member belong to multiple groups?\n* Who may administer groups: owners only, or admins as well?\n* Should personal workspaces support groups?\n* How should group removal affect effective access, pinned skills, or agent configurations?\n* Are nested groups needed, or should the first version remain flat?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-72f905b3b2ce>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-11-support-skill-groups-and-daf45bcc1c17>)",

      "id": "693fecfe-0647-47d3-a152-20874fb3fad5",
      "identifier": "SKI-1",
      "title": "Move service-principal credential authentication to AuthFn API keys",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys",
      "description": "## Context\n\nSkillplane previously owned custom service-principal credential authentication using opaque `sps_...` secrets. AuthFn already provides API-key issuance, hashing, authentication, expiration, and revocation, including a stable API-key actor identity. Skillplane should use that internal capability while continuing to own its service-principal domain model.\n\n## Responsibility split\n\n### AuthFn\n\n* Issue agent credentials.\n* Hash and verify credential secrets.\n* Handle expiration and revocation.\n* Return a stable authenticated actor identity.\n\n### Skillplane\n\n* Map the authenticated actor to a Skillplane service principal.\n* Bind that principal to a workspace.\n* Store and enforce Skillplane-specific roles, scopes, delegation, and domain policy.\n* Record domain audit metadata and lifecycle events.\n* Present credentials to users as Skillplane agent credentials without exposing provider implementation details.\n\nA service principal remains a Skillplane domain entity; only credential lifecycle and authentication are delegated internally.\n\n## Revised product decision\n\nThere is no compatibility window for the former `sps_...` format.\n\n* Removed credentials must fail authentication immediately.\n* The obsolete credential-hash column and fallback verification path must be removed.\n* Existing service-principal records may remain without a usable credential and receive a fresh current credential through the       "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAfter McpFn publishes the upstream Cloudflare Worker packaging fix, Skillplane must upgrade its McpFn dependencies, remove obsolete or temporary MCP Worker compatibility configuration, and verify the full development topology without changing authentication behavior.\n\n## Problem\n\nSkillplane currently consumes `@mcpfn/auth@0.0.4`, `@mcpfn/core@0.0.4`, and `@mcpfn/testing@0.0.4`. Its MCP Worker deployment exposed the mixed `zod` and `zod/v4` startup failure tracked upstream. Skillplane also retains `allow_eval_during_startup` alongside compatibility date `2026-05-03`; local workerd rejects that combination because the behavior is already default for dates on or after 2025-06-01.\n\nThe Worker should consume the corrected McpFn release and use current Cloudflare configuration without retaining a permanent Zod alias, compatibility shim, or redundant flag.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nThe full Skillplane development topology deploy path includes the MCP Worker successfully. Skillplane uses the patched published McpFn packages, generated Wrangler configuration is valid for the configured compatibility date, and existing MCP authentication behavior is preserved.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Upgrade Skillplane to the patched McpFn package release.\n* Remove the obsolete `allow_eval_during_startup` compatibility flag from source and generated MCP Worker configurations.\n* Remove any temporary consumer-side Zod alias or workaround once the upstream package fix is available.\n* Validate the rendered topology, Worker bundle execution, and controlled development deployment.\n* Preserve the existing authenticated MCP endpoint behavior.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Implementing the upstream McpFn or MCP SDK packaging correction.\n* Changing Skillplane tool contracts, tenant policy, or authentication semantics.\n* Production deployment as part of backlog capture.\n* Broad dependency modernization unrelated to this failure.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Skillplane's lockfile resolves the patched published versions of all required McpFn packages.\n* No permanent Skillplane-local `zod/v4` alias or compatibility shim is required.\n* `allow_eval_during_startup` is absent from the source configuration and all rendered topology configurations.\n* The development topology render and deployment checks pass.\n* A real workerd startup test reaches ready state; validation is not limited to Wrangler dry-run bundling.\n* A controlled full development topology deployment includes the MCP Worker without Cloudflare error 10021 or `Class2 is not a constructor`.\n* Smoke validation confirms the deployed MCP endpoint still requires authentication.\n* Validation results clearly distinguish local workerd, Cloudflare development deployment, and production status.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Blocked on the upstream McpFn fix and published package release tracked in MCP-4.\n* Generated Wrangler files must be regenerated from their source templates rather than edited only as outputs.\n* A dependency upgrade could carry unrelated behavior changes; review the release diff and run focused MCP tests.\n* Cloudflare upload validation is an external acceptance layer and must be verified separately from local bundling.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Which patched McpFn version will Skillplane adopt?\n* Are any temporary aliases introduced during incident response present in another branch or deployment environment and therefore need explicit removal?\n* Should the full development topology deployment become a recurring release gate or remain a controlled acceptance check?\n\n## Source context\n\nSupersedes the Skillplane consumer portion of SKI-18: [SKI-18](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-18/fix-cloudflare-dev-mcp-worker-upload-failure)",

      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-16/adopt-ticket-protected-direct-regional-datafn-transport-in-skillplane",
      "description": "## Goal\n\nAfter [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets) are released, move steady-state first-party DataFn reads off the canonical gateway and onto the owning regional DataFn endpoint without weakening authentication, placement fencing, mutation safety, or observability.\n\n## Why\n\n[SKI-13](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-13/refactor-skillplane-into-a-global-control-plane-and-regional-workspace) gives Skillplane canonical placement-aware routing and [SKI-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path) gives the app one typed DataFn read boundary, but every query still traverses the gateway. That preserves correctness while retaining an avoidable cross-region hop. [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) must first expose placement-bound authenticated context, and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets) must first issue short-lived regional transport tickets. This issue is the Skillplane consumer work after those reusable platform contracts exist.\n\n## Implementation sequence\n\n 1. Consume the AuthFn placement-bound authenticated context rather than deriving a second product-local credential model.\n 2. Add one authenticated canonical DataFn bootstrap call at the existing shared app client boundary.\n 3. Resolve the server-owned registry entry and return only an expiry-bound `{ httpUrl, wsUrl, ticket, regionEpoch, expiresAt }` transport grant.\n 4. Expose dedicated public DataFn-only regional endpoints; keep application, AuthFn, MCP, and administrative cell endpoints private.\n 5. Enforce ticket signature, audience, subject, workspace, region, placement epoch, scopes, TTL, CORS, rate limiting, and DDoS controls at every regional endpoint.\n 6. Extend the Skillplane DataFn client transport with in-memory grant caching, proactive renewal, and canonical re-bootstrap on expiry, region/epoch mismatch, workspace movement, or the standard moved-tenant close/error signal.\n 7. Send query, permitted mutation, pull, push, reconcile, and WebSocket sync traffic directly to the owning region. Keep authentication, bootstrap, placement, public projections, and domain commands on the canonical gateway.\n 8. Add per-phase latency and route-provenance telemetry without logging tickets, cookies, or database URLs.\n 9. Add two-region end-to-end tests proving steady-state DataFn traffic bypasses the gateway, placement changes re-bootstrap safely, and mutations are never ambiguously replayed.\n10. Roll out behind a per-environment/per-workspace flag with canary comparison and instant fallback to canonical gateway transport.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* The first authenticated DataFn request bootstraps through the canonical gateway and later requests use the ticket-authorized owning-region endpoint until renewal.\n* Regional endpoints accept no session cookie as authority and reject every ticket mismatch or stale placement epoch.\n* A moved workspace re-bootstrap is automatic and never replays an ambiguous mutation.\n* Auth, public pages, R2/domain commands, MCP, and administrative traffic remain canonical.\n* Two-region browser/integration evidence proves steady-state gateway bypass and measures bootstrap, gateway, regional, DataFn phase, and total latency separately.\n* Rollback switches the shared client boundary back to canonical `/datafn` without feature-level changes.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nBlocked by [AUTH-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) and [DATA-4](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-4/support-gateway-issued-direct-regional-sync-tickets).       "description": "## Goal\n\nOnce the upstream DataFn release is published, upgrade Skillplane to the latest compatible released DataFn packages and remove the local date-serialization workaround.\n\n## Dependency\n\nWait for upstream pending DataFn changes to merge and a release containing the relation-projection date fixes to be published. Upstream publishing is outside this issue. Do not remove the workaround before that release is available.\n\n## Context\n\nSkillplane currently uses @datafn/server 0.1.1. Its relation-projection omission logic can turn Date values into {}. Skillplane compensates with jsonSafeValue and createJsonSafeReadAdapter in packages/datafn/src/server.ts. Upstream dev contains date preservation (5e122f2ae6065dd1f8898031cbf615c265cf36bb) and nested-array omission handling (ff8338238608fe6af1bd898d0f428c205110405b).\n\n## Scope\n\n* Verify the published release contains the upstream fixes and review its compatibility requirements.\n* Bump the relevant DataFn catalog entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml and update pnpm-lock.yaml, keeping related packages compatible.\n* Remove jsonSafeValue/createJsonSafeReadAdapter and obsolete imports/comments; pass the database adapter directly to DataFn.\n* Retain the role-scoped domain model aliases introduced in PR [21nCo/skillplane#16](https://linear.app/21n/review/fix-datafn-model-mappings-in-regional-database-adapters-daae67384487); those fix Skillplane configuration and are not this workaround.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* Skill detail/currentVersion and version-history dates serialize correctly without the wrapper, using both combined and regional adapters.\n* Existing tenant-isolation and mutation-denial coverage remains green; add focused regression coverage where needed for nested relation dates/arrays.\n* Relevant integration tests, type checks, lint and build pass.\n* Dev verification confirms skill detail, SKILL.md content and version history in India, US and EU.\n\nNo upstream DataFn/AuthFn implementation or publishing work is included.",

      "id": "bd8d61d1-715a-4fea-8c0d-0f092c0a6d98",
      "identifier": "SKI-15",
      "title": "Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-15/support-local-first-workspaces-and-resilient-agent-skill-projections",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nBuild a local-first Skillplane client/runtime that works without Skillplane managed cloud while also supporting multiple cloud accounts and workspaces. Users should be able to project Skillplane skills into agent-recognized skill directories for native discovery and slash-command use.\n\nProjected skills should remain self-contained. They carry a versioned embedded snapshot and first prefer the global Skillplane CLI or Skillplane MCP for freshness checks, latest compatible content, and observable invocation analytics. If neither path is available, the agent may use the embedded snapshot with clearly disclosed freshness and analytics limitations.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkillplane currently has strong cloud and MCP workflows, but the desired onboarding and runtime experience spans additional environments:\n\n* individuals who want local workspaces without a managed cloud dependency;\n* nontechnical users who need a one-command installer or desktop-led initialization;\n* developers with multiple local and cloud workspaces across multiple accounts;\n* local agents that discover skills from filesystem directories and expose native slash commands;\n* ephemeral cloud agents that can use Skillplane only through MCP.\n\nStatic skill copies are resilient but become stale and cannot reliably report actual use. A thin runtime-only launcher improves freshness and observed analytics but fails when the CLI, MCP, authentication, or network is unavailable. The product needs a deliberate hybrid rather than a hidden compromise.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nSkillplane becomes usable as one coherent product across local-only, connected local/cloud, native filesystem-agent, and MCP-only ephemeral environments. Workspace authority, projection behavior, freshness policy, trust boundaries, and analytics semantics remain explicit.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Support fully local workspaces without requiring Skillplane managed cloud.\n* Support named cloud account profiles and simultaneous access to local and cloud workspaces.\n* Let a project select one primary write workspace plus zero or more mounted read sources.\n* Project skills atomically into supported agent-specific directories with collision handling and provenance.\n* Use one global Skillplane CLI; do not place resolver executables in every skill folder.\n* Make projected skills self-contained with embedded content, version, digest, source workspace, and trust metadata.\n* Prefer live resolution through the CLI or MCP, then fall back to embedded content without combining conflicting instruction versions.\n* Support resilient, strict-live, and pinned projection policies.\n* Reuse common skill create, retrieve, publish, and amend domain operations across CLI, desktop, API, and MCP.\n* Record honest observed-usage analytics with agent and delivery-mode attribution.\n* Preserve MCP-only operation for ephemeral cloud agents.\n* Keep the installation path compatible with a future one-command bootstrap and desktop setup flow.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Automatic bidirectional replication or conflict-free merging between local and cloud workspace authorities.\n* Guaranteed analytics when an agent uses an embedded snapshot without contacting the CLI or MCP.\n* A per-skill resolver script or daemon packaged into every projected skill.\n* Silent adoption of skill updates that expand scripts, tool permissions, network access, or execution context.\n* A claim that one generic directory or slash-command mechanism works identically across every agent host.\n* Implementation, deployment, assignment, estimates, or delivery dates as part of this backlog capture.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A user can create and use a local workspace offline without a Skillplane cloud account.\n* Credentials for multiple cloud accounts are stored outside project files and workspaces are addressed without slug ambiguity.\n* Project configuration supports one explicit write destination and ordered mounted skill sources.\n* Each supported agent target has a capability-aware projection adapter and documented destination directory.\n* Projection updates are atomic, idempotent, and do not overwrite unrelated user-managed files.\n* A projected skill includes an embedded snapshot plus exact source, version, digest, synchronization time, and policy metadata.\n* The projected instructions define one authoritative source per invocation: live CLI, live MCP, cached CLI, or embedded snapshot.\n* The global CLI can confirm that the embedded digest is current without returning duplicate skill content.\n* A newer permitted version can be returned live and scheduled for projection refresh; offline fallback identifies the cached version and unverified freshness.\n* Updates outside the existing trust envelope require approval rather than silently expanding permissions.\n* Skill creation and amendments behave consistently across local CLI/desktop and cloud MCP transports, using immutable versions and exact-base amendment semantics.\n* MCP-only ephemeral agents can discover, retrieve, create, and amend authorized cloud skills without local filesystem projection.\n* Analytics distinguish projection/install, observed invocation/retrieval, action usage, completion report, and verified success.\n* Usage reporting labels delivery mode and confidence, and does not present unobservable embedded-fallback use as complete totals.\n* Collision, multiple-account, offline, stale-snapshot, permission-expansion, partial-projection, and unavailable-runtime cases have defined behavior and validation coverage.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Agent hosts differ in skill directories, frontmatter, dynamic command execution, MCP support, and slash-command semantics.\n* Instruction-based freshness checks are best effort on hosts without deterministic command injection.\n* Embedding fallback content directly in the main skill body increases context usage and may expose stale and live instructions together; a referenced sibling snapshot may be safer.\n* Live body updates cannot necessarily change already-parsed projection frontmatter or permission declarations.\n* Skill content and bundled scripts are untrusted inputs and require traversal, symlink, size, digest, and execution safeguards.\n* Analytics identity must separate agent product, pseudonymous installation, user identity, and model claims while respecting local privacy choices.\n* Managed-cloud outages and authentication expiry must not corrupt local workspaces or projections.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should the default local store be embedded SQLite plus filesystem content storage?\n* Should resilient projections embed fallback content inline or store it as a sibling snapshot loaded only when needed?\n* Which agent adapters can make the freshness check deterministic, and which remain instruction-driven?\n* Does accepted live content update the projection immediately, on the next sync, or both?\n* What is the default offline policy for managed-team skills: cached fallback or strict failure?\n* How should workspace mounts resolve same-name skills: explicit aliases, namespaces, or ordered precedence?\n* Which analytics are local-only by default, and which may be uploaded after explicit consent?\n* Should local-to-cloud movement remain explicit publish/import operations or later gain an optional replication mode?\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale \u2014 SKI-15: Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-15-support-local-first-workspaces-709fa4e06ec4>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan \u2014 SKI-15: Support local-first workspaces and resilient agent skill projections](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-15-support-local-first-workspaces-9f8209e784e5>)",

      "id": "4a80d045-4bed-40ec-9cad-198aa60b3631",
      "identifier": "SKI-3",
      "title": "Support native skill composition, dependency resolution, and verification modules",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-3/support-native-skill-composition-dependency-resolution-and",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nAdd native, machine-readable skill composition and verification to Skillplane so a published skill can depend on other versioned skills, resolve nested dependency chains deterministically, and provide evidence-based verification requirements to independent verifier agents.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nThe current proof of concept works by placing an exact child-skill selector inside a parent skill's Markdown. Linear successfully followed:\n\n* add-to-backlog 1.1.0 \u2192 create-and-associate-linear-issue 1.0.0\n* issue-fix 1.2.0 \u2192 create-and-associate-linear-issue 1.0.0\n\nThis reduces duplicated instructions, but Skillplane does not represent or enforce the dependency. Agents can ignore it; versions are not resolved as a graph; conflicts, cycles, authorization closure, upgrades, and transitive verification are not native concepts.\n\nVerification is also guidance-only. A skill can ask an agent to use a subsystem such as DataFn, yet an implementation may merely install or scaffold it while routing real reads and mutations around it.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nA composite skill is one logical, immutable Skillplane artifact backed by a locked dependency DAG, deterministic execution plan, inherited verification plan, and evidence-backed attestations tied to the resolved closure and implementation revision.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Introduce a backward-compatible bundle format for execution and verification modules.\n* Declare dependencies by workspace, skill, version constraint, scope, alias, and composition mode.\n* Resolve nested dependencies to exact immutable version IDs and digests.\n* Reject cycles, incompatible constraints, inaccessible dependencies, and visibility widening.\n* Preserve provenance without copying child instructions into every parent.\n* Support include-style composition and structured invocation/handoff dependencies.\n* Give agents a deterministic resolved execution plan.\n* Let skills ship blocking or advisory verification claims and verifier instructions.\n* Compose child verification claims transitively; parents may strengthen but not silently weaken them.\n* Record verification attestations with evidence against a skill closure digest, repository commit, and environment.\n* Surface dependency graphs, closure diffs, upgrade candidates, conflicts, and verification results in UI and MCP.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* Automatically implementing skills or granting broader mutation authority.\n* Silently floating published composites to newer child versions.\n* Treating package installation, imports, or scaffolding as sufficient verification.\n* Concatenating arbitrary Markdown without module boundaries or conflict rules.\n* Assigning owners, estimates, dates, cycles, or implementation priority as part of backlog capture.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* A format-v1 skill continues to behave as an ordinary leaf skill.\n* A format-v2 candidate can declare direct execution and verification dependencies.\n* Candidate creation resolves and records an exact transitive lock; publication revalidates it without silently changing it.\n* Published retrieval returns the root, closure digest, dependency DAG, deterministic execution plan, and verification plan.\n* Resolution rejects cycles, version conflicts, unauthorized nodes, revoked nodes, and configured depth/fan-out/size violations.\n* Dependency upgrades create reviewable parent candidates rather than mutating published versions.\n* Public composites cannot depend on less-visible skills.\n* Verification claims have stable IDs, blocking/advisory severity, scope, required evidence, and pass/fail/unknown semantics.\n* Blocking unknown or failed claims prevent a successful verification attestation.\n* A verifier can independently retrieve the verification closure and attach evidence.\n* The DataFn example fails verification unless every relevant read surface and mutation is inventoried and shown to use DataFn, with bypass detection and representative runtime evidence.\n* UI and MCP expose dependency and verification state without requiring agents to parse prose.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Extends canonical bundle validation, path rules, storage manifests, version persistence, publication, amendment review, authorization, MCP schemas/tools, and skill UI.\n* Requires a server-generated immutable lock and normalized dependency edges.\n* Cross-workspace dependencies require explicit visibility and authorization policy.\n* Archive, deprecation, and revocation need separate semantics so reproducibility and emergency invalidation are not conflated.\n* Resolver output must be bounded against cycles and resource amplification.\n* Verification evidence may contain sensitive implementation data and needs redaction, retention, and access controls.\n* Independent verification is strongest when executor and verifier identities or tool permissions differ.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should MVP permit only same-workspace and public cross-workspace dependencies?\n* Which composition modes ship first: include and invoke only, or an explicit ordered sequence mode too?\n* Should generated lock data live inside the canonical bundle as skill.lock.json, in normalized storage, or both?\n* What default maximum depth, direct dependency count, closure size, and expanded byte size should apply?\n* Does archiving preserve pinned retrieval while a distinct revocation state blocks it?\n* Which verification evidence types should Skillplane understand natively versus store as opaque, hashed references?",

      "id": "829274d3-c021-40ad-8082-91911d541592",
      "identifier": "SKI-10",
      "title": "Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane",
      "url": "https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-10/remove-duplicated-framework-and-security-primitives-from-skillplane",
      "description": "## Executive summary\n\nRefactor Skillplane so released Superfunctions packages own the framework behavior and security primitives they already provide, while Skillplane retains only product-specific policy and domain logic.\n\nThis backlog item captures the remaining actionable findings from the 2026-08-22 repository-wide Superfunctions duplication audit. DataFn adoption is already tracked by [SKI-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path), AuthFn API-key migration by [SKI-1](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys), and McpFn adoption by [SKI-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage); those items are related dependencies and are intentionally not duplicated here.\n\n## Problem or opportunity\n\nSkillplane composes AuthFn, SendFn, DataFn, and shared Superfunctions packages, but several local layers reimplement package-owned behavior:\n\n* custom Hono handlers shadow AuthFn OTP send and verify routes;\n* the browser app reimplements the AuthFn client contract, envelopes, request IDs, validation, session-mode handling, and error mapping;\n* AuthFn Drizzle tables and expected fields are manually mirrored instead of generated;\n* fixed-window persistence duplicates the shared Superfunctions rate-limiter primitive;\n* three signed-cursor implementations duplicate HMAC, base64url, expiry, and filter-binding mechanics;\n* MCP retrieval audit mapping duplicates an exported central helper;\n* the local Cloudflare SendFn adapter is justified, but its custom error hierarchy duplicates SendFn failure contracts.\n\nThese parallel contracts increase drift, security review surface, and migration cost.\n\n## Expected outcome\n\nSkillplane uses native AuthFn routes and clients plus supported hooks/plugins for product policy, generates AuthFn schema deterministically, reuses shared persistence/error contracts where they fit, and has one internal implementation for cursor signing and retrieval audit mapping.\n\n## Goals\n\n* Return OTP route and browser-client ownership to AuthFn.\n* Enforce Turnstile and two-key OTP policy through supported AuthFn hooks or minimal additive middleware.\n* Generate AuthFn schema from the composed plugin set and detect drift in CI.\n* Reuse shared rate-limit persistence while preserving Skillplane's recipient and network policy.\n* Consolidate signed cursor mechanics behind one internal codec with purpose and tenant/filter binding.\n* Remove duplicate MCP retrieval-event mapping.\n* Normalize the local SendFn adapter to native provider response/error contracts.\n* Add focused regression and reachability tests for every migrated boundary.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n* DataFn adoption in first-party app reads; tracked by [SKI-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path).\n* Service-principal API-key migration; tracked by [SKI-1](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys).\n* McpFn registry/transport migration; tracked by [SKI-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage).\n* Replacing Skillplane's OAuth authorization-server plugin, domain services, immutable bundle pipeline, or authorization-aware search.\n* Moving the Cloudflare provider upstream without separate authorization.\n* Assigning people, dates, estimates, or implementation sequencing commitments.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* No Skillplane Hono handler owns the AuthFn OTP send or verify route.\n* The web app consumes the released AuthFn client package instead of a parallel protocol client.\n* Turnstile secrets are transient and never persisted in OTP delivery metadata.\n* Product-specific OTP policy remains fail-closed and has parity tests.\n* AuthFn schema output is deterministic and CI detects generated drift.\n* Generic fixed-window storage is removed or a documented incompatibility explains why shared middleware cannot replace it.\n* One signed-cursor codec owns HMAC/base64url mechanics and uses constant-time verification, expiry, purpose, and tenant/filter binding.\n* MCP retrieval audit mapping has one canonical implementation.\n* SendFn failures use native provider response/error semantics without parallel local error classes.\n* Existing auth, DataFn, email, MCP, and browser-critical regression tests pass.\n* Exact released package versions and supported APIs are reverified before implementation.\n\n## Dependencies and risks\n\n* Related existing issues: [SKI-1](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-1/move-service-principal-credential-authentication-to-authfn-api-keys), [SKI-2](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-2/adopt-datafn-in-skillplanes-first-party-application-data-path), and [SKI-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SKI-6/adopt-mcpfn-for-mcp-regression-and-conformance-coverage).\n* Route migration must preserve cookie-session behavior, request correlation, rate-limit headers where required, and error semantics.\n* The installed AuthFn version has a pre-send hook but may not expose every desired pre-verify or response-header hook.\n* Schema generation requires migration review to avoid destructive database drift.\n* Cursor consolidation is security-sensitive and requires compatibility or explicit invalidation decisions.\n* Shared rate-limit adapters may need an upstream extension for the current persistence model.\n\n## Open questions\n\n* Should additive OTP response headers be implemented by thin response middleware or proposed as an upstream AuthFn hook?\n* Should existing cursors remain valid during migration, or can the deployment intentionally invalidate them?\n* Does shared rate-limit persistence support the required Postgres behavior directly, or is a small upstream adapter needed?\n* Should the Cloudflare SendFn provider move upstream in a separate Superfunctions issue after local normalization?\n\n## Evidence\n\nSource audit: `.conduct/audits/2026-08-22-df2a110c-full-audit.md`\n\nAudit snapshot: branch `codex/local-dev-oauth`, commit `45733752797a5de552a447560983d24a9d02bcd1`. The audit was read-only and did not claim browser, database, tunnel, deployed, or production verification.\n\n## Supporting documents\n\n* [Ideation & Product Rationale \u2014 SKI-10: Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane](<https://linear.app/21n/document/ideation-and-product-rationale-ski-10-remove-duplicated-framework-and-6b49cd027863>)\n* [Architecture & Delivery Plan \u2014 SKI-10: Remove duplicated framework and security primitives from Skillplane](<https://linear.app/21n/document/architecture-and-delivery-plan-ski-10-remove-duplicated-framework-and-58a68c622bf3>)",
